question: Does the PR-173 scripted first-line precheck reduce latency in the VARE edit-apply path while preserving every observed output?

task.generator: deterministic seeded public generator; 800-2500 line source files; 1-3 edit blocks; varied exact/relaxed/missing/ambiguous cases

arms.scripted_known_good: PR-173 known_good.patch, independently verified through vare.isolated_candidate
arms.scripted_incorrect: relaxed matcher returns None for every call; correctness control only
arms.model_attempt_1: Qwen3-4B local proposal; rejected on correctness before timing
arms.model_attempt_2: AST-equivalent duplicate of attempt 1; rejected without a second execution

evaluation_boundary.expected_outputs: computed by the unchanged parent module; candidate never receives expected values or grader files
evaluation_boundary.null_transport: represent optional new_text as has_new_text plus a string field because frozen isolated_candidate.values_close does not compare JSON null values

measurement.primary: geometric mean of five paired ratios of per-call parent-clock request-response means; lower two-sided 95% Student-t interval must exceed 1.0 and point estimate must be >=1.05
measurement.per_call_interval: parent request write to trusted response frame receipt inside a warmed session container; subject import and container startup are excluded
measurement.secondary: outer wall time per session, including worker and container startup
measurement.noise_floor_rule: A/A mean-difference 95% interval must contain zero; otherwise report measurement invalid
stopping_rules: any baseline or candidate output mismatch

exposure.model_prompt: only the target source and public task/tests; no control patch, generated inputs, expected outputs, or held-out tests
